• He said: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿wa-ẓillin mamdūd﴾. Qatadah said: "Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without cutting through it.'"

• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without cutting through it."

• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, the like of that also.

* *

His saying: ﴿and water poured forth﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: and in it there is also flowing water, meaning poured out, flowing in no trench.

As:

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, regarding ﴿wa-māʾin maskūb﴾: "It flows in no trench."

**The interpretation of His saying (Exalted is He):** ﴿And the companions of the right hand — what are the companions of the right hand?﴾ ﴿Among lote-trees without thorns,﴾ ﴿and acacias layered with fruit,﴾ ﴿and extended shade,﴾ ﴿and water poured forth.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And the companions of the right hand﴾, who are those who will be taken on the Day of Resurrection to the right, those who were given their records in their right hands, O Muhammad. ﴿What are the companions of the right hand?﴾ What they are, what their state is, and what good has been prepared for them. It has also been said that they are the children of the believers.

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to us, saying: Abu Hisham al-Makhzumi narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Qays narrated to us, that he heard Zadhan Abu Amr say: I heard Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) say: ﴿And the companions of the right hand, what are the companions of the right hand?﴾ He said: "The companions of the right hand are the children of the believers."

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And the companions of the right hand, what are the companions of the right hand?﴾ He said: that is, what is their state, and what has been prepared for them. Then he began the report about what has been prepared for them in Paradise, and what their condition will be when they enter it, so He said: they are ﴿among lote-trees without thorns﴾, meaning: among fruit of lote-trees laden with fruit, whose thorns have been removed.

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil, those who engage in ta'wil, i.e., interpretation of the Qur'an) differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said: what is meant by "khudud" (without thorns) is that which has been stripped of thorns, so there are no thorns on it.

Mention of those who said this:

• Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿among lote-trees without thorns﴾, he said: "He stripped it and made it heavy with fruit. It is said: it was stripped until its thorns disappeared, so there are no thorns on it."

• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father: ﴿among lote-trees without thorns﴾, he said: Muhammad ibn Ikrimah claimed, saying: "There are no thorns on it."

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib, from Ikrimah, regarding His saying: ﴿among lote-trees without thorns﴾, he said: "There are no thorns on it."

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdhah ibn Khalifah narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from Qassamah ibn Zuhayr, regarding His saying: ﴿among lote-trees without thorns﴾, he said: "It was stripped of thorns, so there are no thorns on it."

• Abu Humayd al-Himsi Ahmad ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Amr ibn Abd Allah al-Ahmusi narrated to us, from al-Safr ibn Nusayr, regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿among lote-trees without thorns﴾, he said: "Its thorns were stripped, so there are no thorns on it."

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, His saying: ﴿among lote-trees without thorns﴾, he said: "We used to be told that it is the heavily laden one that has no thorns."

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Qatadah narrated to us, regarding His saying: ﴿among lote-trees without thorns﴾, he said: "There are no thorns on it."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas: ﴿among lote-trees without thorns﴾, he said: "It has no thorns."

• Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Ikrimah: ﴿among lote-trees without thorns﴾, he said: "There are no thorns on it."

• Ibn Humayd narrated this to me again, another time, from Mihran, with this chain, from Ikrimah, and he said: "It has no thorns, and it is laden with fruit."

Others said: rather, what is meant by it is that it is heavy with fruit.

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿khudud (stripped)﴾, he said: "They say: this is the one heavy with fruit."

• Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿among lote-trees without thorns﴾, he said: "The heavily laden one."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿among lote-trees without thorns﴾, he said: "The heavily laden one."

• It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying: ﴿among lote-trees without thorns﴾: "Heavily laden."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿among lote-trees without thorns﴾, he said: "Its fruit is larger than the large earthen jars (qilal)."

* *

His saying: ﴿and acacias layered with fruit﴾

As for al-Farra', he read it with the "ha'" (ḥ): ﴿wa-ṭalḥin manḍūd﴾, and it is thus in the codices of the people of the regions. It is narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) that he used to read ﴿wa-ṭalʿin manḍūd﴾ with the "ayn" (ʿ), i.e., "wa-ṭalʿin" meaning "banana clusters" (in place of "ṭalḥ," meaning acacia).

• Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Zakariyya narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'd, from his father (may Allah be pleased with him), that he read it as ﴿wa-ṭalʿin manḍūd﴾.

• Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: Mujahid narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'd, from Qays ibn Sa'd, who said: A man recited ﴿wa-ṭalḥin manḍūd﴾ in the presence of Ali, and Ali said: "What is the matter with ṭalḥ? It is only ṭalʿ," and then he recited ﴿its spathe (ṭalʿuhā) is soft﴾. We said: "Shall we change it?" He said: "The Qur'an is not to be altered today, nor changed." As for ṭalḥ, al-Mu'ammar ibn al-Muthanna used to say: among the Arabs it is a large tree with many thorns, and he recited a verse of one of the camel-drivers (ḥudāh):

*"Her guide gave her good news and said: 'Tomorrow you will see the acacias and the sand-dunes.'"*

[Footnote: This is one of the verses cited by Abu Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 175, from the photographed copy of the manuscript "Murad Muntla" in Istanbul). He recited it at the saying of Allah, "wa-ṭalḥin manḍūd," and said: "The interpreters claim it is the banana; but the Arabs use ṭalḥ for a large tree with many thorns." The camel-driver said: "Her guide gave her good news..." (the two verses). As for "al-ḥibāl" with the ḥā' as in the narration of the author, it is the plural of ḥabl, which is a raised sand-dune that extends a long distance across the earth; with the jīm, as in Abu Ubaydah's narration, it is the plural of jabal (mountain). He gives the good news to his she-camel that she will reach her homeland tomorrow and see in it the acacia trees she is accustomed to, and the sand-dunes or mountains.]

As for the interpreters among the Companions and the Successors (tabi'un), they say that it is the banana.

• Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Sulayman al-Taymi narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id, client of Banu Raqqash, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about ṭalḥ, and he said: "It is the banana."

• Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Sulayman al-Taymi informed us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Raqqashi narrated to us, that he heard Ibn Abbas say: "Ṭalḥ manḍūd: it is the banana."

• Ya'qub and Abu Kurayb narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Sulayman, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Raqqashi narrated to us, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas: "What is ṭalḥ manḍūd?" He said: "It is the banana."

• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Raqqashi narrated to us, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about ṭalḥ, and he said: "It is the banana."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Taymi, from Abu Sa'id al-Raqqashi, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿wa-ṭalḥin manḍūd﴾: "The banana."

• He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Kalbi, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding ﴿wa-ṭalḥin manḍūd﴾: "The banana."

• Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Bishr informed us, from a man from Basra, who heard Ibn Abbas say regarding ṭalḥ manḍūd: "It is the banana."

• Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿wa-ṭalḥin manḍūd﴾, he said: "Your banana, because they used to admire the shade of the (wajj) tree and its shadows from among its acacias and lote-trees."

• Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Ata', regarding His saying: ﴿wa-ṭalḥin manḍūd﴾, he said: "The banana."

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdhah ibn Khalifah narrated to us, from Awf, from Qassamah, who said: "Ṭalḥ manḍūd: it is the banana."

• He said: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding the saying of Allah ﴿wa-ṭalḥin manḍūd﴾, he said: "The banana." Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿wa-ṭalḥin manḍūd﴾, he said: "The banana."

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿wa-ṭalḥin manḍūd﴾: "We used to be told that it is the banana."

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿wa-ṭalḥin manḍūd﴾: "Allah knows best, except that the people of Yemen call the banana ṭalḥ."

* *

His saying: ﴿manḍūd (layered)﴾

That is, some of it is arranged upon others, and some of it is gathered together with other parts.

The interpreters have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿wa-ṭalḥin manḍūd﴾: "Some of it upon others."

• al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿wa-ṭalḥin manḍūd﴾: "Piled up, because they admire the shade of the (wajj) tree and its shadows, from its acacia and its lote-trees."

* *

His saying: ﴿and extended shade﴾

He says: they will be in a constant shade that the sun does not cancel out so as to destroy it. Everything that has no end is "mamdūd" (extended), as Labid said:

*"Time, long and enduring and extended, overcame survival, though I was not one to be overcome."*

[Footnote: The verse is by Labid. Abu Ubaydah attributed it to him in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 175b), and in his narration it reads "al-ghurrā'" instead of "al-baqā'" in the author's narration. The meaning: the long time overcame survival in this world, and nothing would overcome me except time. Abu Ubaydah recited it at the saying of Allah, "wa-ẓillin mamdūd," and said: "That is, the sun does not cancel it; it is constant. 'Mamdūd' is said of a long time or a life that does not end." Labid said: "Overcame survival..." (the verse).]

The traditions came with something similar to what we have said regarding this, and the scholars have held this view.

Mention of those who said this:

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun, regarding ﴿wa-ẓillin mamdūd﴾: "Five hundred thousand years."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from Ziyad, client of Banu Makhzum, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years. Recite, if you wish: ﴿wa-ẓillin mamdūd﴾." This reached Ka'b, who said: "He spoke the truth. By Him who sent down the Torah upon the tongue of Musa and the Furqan upon the tongue of Muhammad, if a man were to ride a young she-camel (ḥuqqah) or a four-year-old camel (jadh'ah) and circle around the root of that tree, he would not reach it until he fell down aged. Allah planted it with His hand and breathed into it of His spirit. Its branches extend beyond the wall of Paradise, and there is no river in Paradise but it flows out from the root of that tree."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Ziyad, client of Banu Makhzum, that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: "and there is no river in Paradise."

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun, regarding ﴿wa-ẓillin mamdūd﴾: "A journey of seventy thousand years."

• Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Yahya ibn Sulayman informed me, from Hilal ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Amrah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years. Recite, if you wish: ﴿wa-ẓillin mamdūd﴾."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ziyad, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years. Recite, if you wish: ﴿wa-ẓillin mamdūd﴾."

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ziyad, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "And indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without cutting through it. Recite, if you wish: ﴿wa-ẓillin mamdūd﴾."

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu al-Duha, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without cutting through it, without cutting through it; it is the tree of eternity (shajarat al-khuld)."

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, who said: I heard Abu al-Dahhak narrate, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "And indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for seventy or a hundred years; it is the tree of eternity."

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Imran narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without cutting through it."

• He said: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Imran narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of that.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of it.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abdah and Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without cutting through it. Recite, if you wish, His saying: ﴿wa-ẓillin mamdūd﴾."

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Firdaws narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years."

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the like of that.

• Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: "It reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without cutting through it.'"

• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Khalid narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and the like of it from Khallas.

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, saying: Abu Husayn narrated to us, who said: We were at a door in a certain place, and with us were Abu Salih and Shaqiq, meaning al-Dabbi. Abu Salih narrated, saying: "Abu Hurayrah told me: 'Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for seventy years.'" Shaqiq said: "Do you call Abu Hurayrah a liar?" Abu Salih said: "I do not call Abu Hurayrah a liar, but I call you a liar." He said: "That was grievous to the reciters (qurra') that day."

• Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿wa-ẓillin mamdūd﴾, he said: "It was narrated to us from Anas ibn Malik, who said: 'Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without cutting through it.'"

• He said: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿wa-ẓillin mamdūd﴾. Qatadah said: "Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without cutting through it.'"

• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without cutting through it."

• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, the like of that also.

* *

His saying: ﴿and water poured forth﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: and in it there is also flowing water, meaning poured out, flowing in no trench.

As:

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, regarding ﴿wa-māʾin maskūb﴾: "It flows in no trench."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 56, verses 32–38:

The explanation of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And fruit in abundance, neither cut off nor forbidden, and raised couches, indeed We have produced them with a special production, and made them virgins, loving (ʿurub), equal in age, for the companions of the right hand.﴾

He says, ﴿And fruit in abundance, neither cut off nor forbidden﴾: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: therein is ﴿fruit in abundance﴾, none of which is cut off from them at any time they desire it, as the fruits of summer are cut off in winter in this world, and none of which is forbidden to them, nor does thorn on its trees or its distance from them come between them and it, as the fruits of this world are withheld from many who desire them, either by their distance on the tree from them or by the thorns on its branches. Rather, when one of them desires it, it falls into his mouth or draws near to him until he takes it with his hand.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said concerning this.

We have already mentioned the narrations on this before, and we will mention some others from them:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, saying: Qatadah narrated to us, concerning His words, ﴿neither cut off nor forbidden﴾, he said: Neither thorn nor distance prevents him from it.

* *

And His words: ﴿and raised couches﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: For them therein are raised couches, long, one above another, as one says: a raised (marfuʿ) building.

Like what has been said:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Rushdin ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn al-Harith, from Darraj Abu al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His words ﴿and raised couches﴾, he said: "Indeed their height is like what is between the heaven and the earth, and what is between the heaven and the earth is a journey of five hundred years."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ﴿and raised couches﴾: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, indeed their height. . ." Then he mentioned the like of it.

* *

And His words: ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production. So We made them virgins, loving﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed We created them with a creation, We brought them into being. Abu ʿUbaydah said: By this is meant the ḥūr ʿīn (wide-eyed maidens) whom He mentioned before, when He said ﴿and wide-eyed maidens like hidden pearls, a reward for what they used to do﴾ and ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾. Al-Akhfash said: He concealed them (in the pronoun) and did not mention them before that.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾, he said: We created them as a creation.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Shaybān, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Yazid ibn Murrah, from Salamah ibn Yazid, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning this verse, ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾, he said: "Of the previously married and the virgins."

* *

And His words: ﴿So We made them virgins﴾

He says: We made them virgins, maidens, after they had been (old women).[[Perhaps he omitted the predicate of "kunna" relying on its explicit mention in the following hadith; i.e., after they had been old women.]]

As:

Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mahran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Musa ibn ʿUbaydah, from Yazid ibn Aban al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾, he said: "Old women who were in this world blear-eyed and with discharge from the eyes."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mahran narrated to us, from Musa ibn ʿUbaydah, from Yazid ibn Aban al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed We have produced them with a special production", he said: He produced old women who were in this world blear-eyed and with discharge from the eyes.

ʿUmar ibn Ismaʿil ibn Mujalid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Rabiʿah al-Kilabi narrated to us, from Musa ibn ʿUbaydah al-Rabadhi, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, concerning His words ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾, he said: "Among them are the old women who were in this world blear-eyed and with discharge from the eyes."

Sawwar ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Dawud narrated to us, from Musa ibn ʿUbaydah al-Rabadhi, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His words ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾, he said: "They are those who were in this world old women, blear-eyed and with discharge from the eyes."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir narrated to us, from his father, from Qatadah, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, concerning His words ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production. So We made them virgins﴾, he said: They are the decrepit, blear-eyed old women.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, saying: Qatadah narrated to us, concerning His words ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production. So We made them virgins﴾, he said: Among them are the decrepit, trembling old women, whom Allah produced in this creation.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾. Qatadah said: Safwan ibn Muhriz used to say: Among them are the decrepit trembling old women, whom Allah transformed as you hear.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: His words ﴿virgins﴾ mean: maidens.

Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Sadafi al-Dimyati narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi Karimah, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Umm Salamah, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, that she said: I said, O Messenger of Allah, inform me about the saying of Allah ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production. So We made them virgins, loving, equal in age, for the companions of the right hand﴾. He said: "They are those who were taken in this world as old women, blear-eyed, white-haired; Allah created them after old age and made them maidens."

Abu ʿUbayd al-Wassabi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayr narrated to us, saying: Thabit ibn ʿAjlan narrated to us, saying: I heard Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrate from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production. So We made them virgins, loving, equal in age﴾, he said: They are of the children of Adam; your women in this world, Allah produces them as virgins, maidens, loving.

* *

And His words: ﴿ʿurub﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So We made them virgins, glancing coquettishly (ghanijāt), loving toward their husbands, graceful in their conjugal relations. It is a plural; its singular is ʿarūb, just as the singular of rusul is rasūl and the singular of qutūf is qatūf. From this is the verse of Labid:

"And in the litters is an ʿarūb, not vulgar, with full hips, whose glance is dazzled by her."

[[This verse is by the poet Labid; Abu ʿUbaydah attributes it to him in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 175b), reciting it at His words "ʿurub atrāban", saying: its singular is ʿarūb, meaning the good in marital devotion (affection toward the husband). The verse's version in Fath al-Qadir of al-Shawkani (5:149): "Rayya al-rawadif yu'shi ḍawuʾhā al-basara."]]

Like what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation have said:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from al-Mubarak ibn Fudalah, from al-Hasan, who said: those who desire their husbands.

He said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: ʿUthman ibn al-Aswad informed us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUbayd Allah, who said: the ʿurub: she who desires her husband.

Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Sadafi al-Dimyati narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Hashim, from Abu Karimah, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from al-Hasan, from his mother, from Umm Salamah, who said: I said, O Messenger of Allah, inform me about His words ﴿ʿurub atrāban﴾. He said: "ʿurub, passionately loving, affectionate; atrāban, of one age."

The reciters differed in the reading of this. Some reciters of Madinah and some reciters of Kufa read ʿurubā with a damma on the ʿayn and the rāʾ. Some reciters of Kufa and Basra read ﴿wa-ʿurubā﴾ with a damma on the ʿayn and a light rāʾ, and this is the dialect of Tamim and Bakr. The damma in both instances is the more correct of the two readings, for the reason I have mentioned, that it is the plural of ʿarūb; and when fa'ūl, fa'īl or fi'āl is pluralized, it is pluralized as fu'ul with a damma on the fāʾ and ʿayn, whether masculine or feminine. Lightening the ʿayn is permissible, though what I have mentioned is the more eloquent form of the lightened reading.

* *

And His words: ﴿atrāban﴾

It means that they are of equal age, of one age; its singular is tirb, as one says: shabah and ashbāh.

Like what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation have said:

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah ﴿atrāban﴾, meaning: one age.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to me, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, similarly.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: concerning His words ﴿atrāban﴾, he said: al-atrāb: the equal ones.

* *

And His words: ﴿for the companions of the right hand﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We produced these whose description of virgins He has stated, for those who will be taken on the right side (dhāt al-yamīn) from the place of reckoning to Paradise.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 56, verses 32–38:

The explanation of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And fruit in abundance, neither cut off nor forbidden, and raised couches, indeed We have produced them with a special production, and made them virgins, loving (ʿurub), equal in age, for the companions of the right hand.﴾

He says, ﴿And fruit in abundance, neither cut off nor forbidden﴾: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: therein is ﴿fruit in abundance﴾, none of which is cut off from them at any time they desire it, as the fruits of summer are cut off in winter in this world, and none of which is forbidden to them, nor does thorn on its trees or its distance from them come between them and it, as the fruits of this world are withheld from many who desire them, either by their distance on the tree from them or by the thorns on its branches. Rather, when one of them desires it, it falls into his mouth or draws near to him until he takes it with his hand.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said concerning this.

We have already mentioned the narrations on this before, and we will mention some others from them:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, saying: Qatadah narrated to us, concerning His words, ﴿neither cut off nor forbidden﴾, he said: Neither thorn nor distance prevents him from it.

* *

And His words: ﴿and raised couches﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: For them therein are raised couches, long, one above another, as one says: a raised (marfuʿ) building.

Like what has been said:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Rushdin ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn al-Harith, from Darraj Abu al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His words ﴿and raised couches﴾, he said: "Indeed their height is like what is between the heaven and the earth, and what is between the heaven and the earth is a journey of five hundred years."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ﴿and raised couches﴾: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, indeed their height. . ." Then he mentioned the like of it.

And His words: ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production. So We made them virgins, loving﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed We created them with a creation, We brought them into being. Abu ʿUbaydah said: By this is meant the ḥūr ʿīn (wide-eyed maidens) whom He mentioned before, when He said ﴿and wide-eyed maidens like hidden pearls, a reward for what they used to do﴾ and ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾. Al-Akhfash said: He concealed them (in the pronoun) and did not mention them before that.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salim al-Aftas, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, similarly.

And His words: ﴿for the companions of the right hand﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We produced these whose description of virgins He has stated, for those who will be taken on the right side (dhāt al-yamīn) from the place of reckoning to Paradise.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 56, verses 32–38:

The explanation of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And fruit in abundance, neither cut off nor forbidden, and raised couches, indeed We have produced them with a special production, and made them virgins, loving (ʿurub), equal in age, for the companions of the right hand.﴾

He says, ﴿And fruit in abundance, neither cut off nor forbidden﴾: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: therein is ﴿fruit in abundance﴾, none of which is cut off from them at any time they desire it, as the fruits of summer are cut off in winter in this world, and none of which is forbidden to them, nor does thorn on its trees or its distance from them come between them and it, as the fruits of this world are withheld from many who desire them, either by their distance on the tree from them or by the thorns on its branches. Rather, when one of them desires it, it falls into his mouth or draws near to him until he takes it with his hand.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said concerning this.

We have already mentioned the narrations on this before, and we will mention some others from them:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, saying: Qatadah narrated to us, concerning His words, ﴿neither cut off nor forbidden﴾, he said: Neither thorn nor distance prevents him from it.

* *

And His words: ﴿and raised couches﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: For them therein are raised couches, long, one above another, as one says: a raised (marfuʿ) building.

Like what has been said:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Rushdin ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn al-Harith, from Darraj Abu al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His words ﴿and raised couches﴾, he said: "Indeed their height is like what is between the heaven and the earth, and what is between the heaven and the earth is a journey of five hundred years."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ﴿and raised couches﴾: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, indeed their height. . ." Then he mentioned the like of it.

And His words: ﴿ʿurub﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So We made them virgins, glancing coquettishly (ghanijāt), loving toward their husbands, graceful in their conjugal relations. It is a plural; its singular is ʿarūb, just as the singular of rusul is rasūl and the singular of qutūf is qatūf. From this is the verse of Labid:

"And in the litters is an ʿarūb, not vulgar, with full hips, whose glance is dazzled by her."

[[This verse is by the poet Labid; Abu ʿUbaydah attributes it to him in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 175b), reciting it at His words "ʿurub atrāban", saying: its singular is ʿarūb, meaning the good in marital devotion (affection toward the husband). Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, saying: Qatadah narrated to us, concerning His words, ﴿neither cut off nor forbidden﴾, he said: Neither thorn nor distance prevents him from it.

* *

And His words: ﴿and raised couches﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: For them therein are raised couches, long, one above another, as one says: a raised (marfuʿ) building.

Like what has been said:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Rushdin ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn al-Harith, from Darraj Abu al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His words ﴿and raised couches﴾, he said: "Indeed their height is like what is between the heaven and the earth, and what is between the heaven and the earth is a journey of five hundred years."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ﴿and raised couches﴾: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, indeed their height. . ." Then he mentioned the like of it.

* *

And His words: ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production. So We made them virgins, loving﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed We created them with a creation, We brought them into being. Abu ʿUbaydah said: By this is meant the ḥūr ʿīn (wide-eyed maidens) whom He mentioned before, when He said ﴿and wide-eyed maidens like hidden pearls, a reward for what they used to do﴾ and ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾. Al-Akhfash said: He concealed them (in the pronoun) and did not mention them before that.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾, he said: We created them as a creation.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Shaybān, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Yazid ibn Murrah, from Salamah ibn Yazid, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning this verse, ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾, he said: "Of the previously married and the virgins."

* *

And His words: ﴿So We made them virgins﴾

He says: We made them virgins, maidens, after they had been (old women).[[Perhaps he omitted the predicate of "kunna" relying on its explicit mention in the following hadith; i.e., after they had been old women.]]

As:

Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mahran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Musa ibn ʿUbaydah, from Yazid ibn Aban al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾, he said: "Old women who were in this world blear-eyed and with discharge from the eyes."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mahran narrated to us, from Musa ibn ʿUbaydah, from Yazid ibn Aban al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed We have produced them with a special production", he said: He produced old women who were in this world blear-eyed and with discharge from the eyes.

ʿUmar ibn Ismaʿil ibn Mujalid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Rabiʿah al-Kilabi narrated to us, from Musa ibn ʿUbaydah al-Rabadhi, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, concerning His words ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾, he said: "Among them are the old women who were in this world blear-eyed and with discharge from the eyes."

Sawwar ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Dawud narrated to us, from Musa ibn ʿUbaydah al-Rabadhi, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His words ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾, he said: "They are those who were in this world old women, blear-eyed and with discharge from the eyes."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir narrated to us, from his father, from Qatadah, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, concerning His words ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production. So We made them virgins﴾, he said: They are the decrepit, blear-eyed old women.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, saying: Qatadah narrated to us, concerning His words ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production. So We made them virgins﴾, he said: Among them are the decrepit, trembling old women, whom Allah produced in this creation.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾. Qatadah said: Safwan ibn Muhriz used to say: Among them are the decrepit trembling old women, whom Allah transformed as you hear.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: His words ﴿virgins﴾ mean: maidens.

Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Sadafi al-Dimyati narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi Karimah, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Umm Salamah, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, that she said: I said, O Messenger of Allah, inform me about the saying of Allah ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production. So We made them virgins, loving, equal in age, for the companions of the right hand﴾. He said: "They are those who were taken in this world as old women, blear-eyed, white-haired; Allah created them after old age and made them maidens."

Abu ʿUbayd al-Wassabi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayr narrated to us, saying: Thabit ibn ʿAjlan narrated to us, saying: I heard Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrate from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production. So We made them virgins, loving, equal in age﴾, he said: They are of the children of Adam; your women in this world, Allah produces them as virgins, maidens, loving.

* *

And His words: ﴿ʿurub﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So We made them virgins, glancing coquettishly (ghanijāt), loving toward their husbands, graceful in their conjugal relations. It is a plural; its singular is ʿarūb, just as the singular of rusul is rasūl and the singular of qutūf is qatūf. From this is the verse of Labid:

"And in the litters is an ʿarūb, not vulgar, with full hips, whose glance is dazzled by her."

Like what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation have said:

Mention of those who said that:

ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His words ﴿ʿurub﴾, he says: ʿawashiq (passionately loving).

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: al-ʿurub are the ones who are coquettish and affectionate toward their husbands.

Sulayman ibn ʿUbayd Allah al-Ghaylani narrated to me, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Qurrah informed us, from al-Hasan, who said: al-ʿurub: the one who loves passionately.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Simak, from ʿIkrimah, that he said concerning this verse, ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: al-ʿurub: the coquettish ones (al-maghnūjah).

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Simak ibn ʿIkrimah, who said: They are the coquettish ones (al-maghnūjah).

Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, saying: ʿUmarah ibn Abi Hafsah narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, concerning His words ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: coquettish (ghinjāt).

ʿAli ibn al-Hasan al-Azdi narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq al-Taymi, from Salih ibn Hayyan, from Abu Buraydah ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: al-shaklah in the dialect of Makkah, and al-ghinjah in the dialect of Madinah.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: I heard Ibrahim al-Taymi, i.e., Ibn al-Zabarqan, from Salih ibn Hayyan, from Abu Yazid, with similar.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from ʿUthman ibn Bashshar, from Tamim ibn Hadhlam, concerning His words ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: the good conjugal relations of the woman.

Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from ʿUthman ibn Bashshar, from Tamim ibn Hadhlam, concerning ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: al-ʿaribah: the one good in conjugal relations. He said: The Arabs used to say of a woman when she was good in conjugal relations: "Indeed she is ʿarībah."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Usamah ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: good in speech.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, who said: ʿawashiq.

He said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Shareek, from Khusayf, from Mujahid and ʿIkrimah, similarly.

He said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Husayn, from Mujahid concerning ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: the ʿurub are the affectionate ones.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: the ʿurub: the ʿawashiq.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salim al-Aftas, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, similarly.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ghalib Abu al-Hudhayl, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: the ʿurub are those who desire their husbands.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from al-Mubarak ibn Fudalah, from al-Hasan, who said: those who desire their husbands.

He said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: ʿUthman ibn al-Aswad informed us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUbayd Allah, who said: the ʿurub: she who desires her husband.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from ʿUthman ibn al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: the ʿarībah: she who desires her husband. Do you not see that a man says of a she-camel: "Indeed she is ʿarībah"?

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: ʿushshaq (passionately loving) toward their husbands.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, His words ﴿ʿurub atrāban﴾, he says: ʿushshaq toward their husbands, loving their husbands with intense love.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: al-ʿurub: those who show affection.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿ʿurub atrāban﴾, he said: affectionate toward their husbands.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: al-ʿurub: good in speech.

Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, saying: al-Awza'i was asked about ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: I heard Yahya say: they are the ʿawashiq.

Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Sadafi al-Dimyati narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Hashim, from Abu Karimah, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from al-Hasan, from his mother, from Umm Salamah, who said: I said, O Messenger of Allah, inform me about His words ﴿ʿurub atrāban﴾. He said: "ʿurub, passionately loving, affectionate; atrāban, of one age."

Muhammad ibn Hafs Abu ʿUbayd al-Wassabi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayr narrated to us, saying: Thabit ibn ʿAjlan narrated to us, saying: I heard Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrate from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿ʿurub﴾, and al-ʿarab: the longing (al-shawq).

The reciters differed in the reading of this. Some reciters of Madinah and some reciters of Kufa read ʿurubā with a damma on the ʿayn and the rāʾ. Some reciters of Kufa and Basra read ﴿wa-ʿurubā﴾ with a damma on the ʿayn and a light rāʾ, and this is the dialect of Tamim and Bakr. The damma in both instances is the more correct of the two readings, for the reason I have mentioned, that it is the plural of ʿarūb; and when fa'ūl, fa'īl or fi'āl is pluralized, it is pluralized as fu'ul with a damma on the fāʾ and ʿayn, whether masculine or feminine. Lightening the ʿayn is permissible, though what I have mentioned is the more eloquent form of the lightened reading.

* *

And His words: ﴿atrāban﴾

It means that they are of equal age, of one age; its singular is tirb, as one says: shabah and ashbāh.

Like what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation have said:

Mention of those who said that:

ʿAli ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Rabiʿah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Sabur, from ʿAtiyyah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: al-atrāb: the equal ones.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, His words ﴿atrāban﴾, he said: likenesses.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah ﴿atrāban﴾, meaning: one age.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to me, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, similarly.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: concerning His words ﴿atrāban﴾, he said: al-atrāb: the equal ones.

* *

And His words: ﴿for the companions of the right hand﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We produced these whose description of virgins He has stated, for those who will be taken on the right side (dhāt al-yamīn) from the place of reckoning to Paradise.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 56, verses 32–38:

The explanation of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And fruit in abundance, neither cut off nor forbidden, and raised couches, indeed We have produced them with a special production, and made them virgins, loving (ʿurub), equal in age, for the companions of the right hand.﴾

He says, ﴿And fruit in abundance, neither cut off nor forbidden﴾: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: therein is ﴿fruit in abundance﴾, none of which is cut off from them at any time they desire it, as the fruits of summer are cut off in winter in this world, and none of which is forbidden to them, nor does thorn on its trees or its distance from them come between them and it, as the fruits of this world are withheld from many who desire them, either by their distance on the tree from them or by the thorns on its branches. Rather, when one of them desires it, it falls into his mouth or draws near to him until he takes it with his hand.

The reciters differed in the reading of this. Some reciters of Madinah and some reciters of Kufa read ʿurubā with a damma on the ʿayn and the rāʾ. Some reciters of Kufa and Basra read ﴿wa-ʿurubā﴾ with a damma on the ʿayn and a light rāʾ, and this is the dialect of Tamim and Bakr. It means that they are of equal age, of one age; its singular is tirb, as one says: shabah and ashbāh.

And His words: ﴿for the companions of the right hand﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We produced these whose description of virgins He has stated, for those who will be taken on the right side (dhāt al-yamīn) from the place of reckoning to Paradise.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 56, verses 32–38:

The explanation of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And fruit in abundance, neither cut off nor forbidden, and raised couches, indeed We have produced them with a special production, and made them virgins, loving (ʿurub), equal in age, for the companions of the right hand.﴾

He says, ﴿And fruit in abundance, neither cut off nor forbidden﴾: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: therein is ﴿fruit in abundance﴾, none of which is cut off from them at any time they desire it, as the fruits of summer are cut off in winter in this world, and none of which is forbidden to them, nor does thorn on its trees or its distance from them come between them and it, as the fruits of this world are withheld from many who desire them, either by their distance on the tree from them or by the thorns on its branches. Rather, when one of them desires it, it falls into his mouth or draws near to him until he takes it with his hand.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said concerning this.

We have already mentioned the narrations on this before, and we will mention some others from them:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, saying: Qatadah narrated to us, concerning His words, ﴿neither cut off nor forbidden﴾, he said: Neither thorn nor distance prevents him from it.

* *

And His words: ﴿and raised couches﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: For them therein are raised couches, long, one above another, as one says: a raised (marfuʿ) building.

Like what has been said:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Rushdin ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn al-Harith, from Darraj Abu al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His words ﴿and raised couches﴾, he said: "Indeed their height is like what is between the heaven and the earth, and what is between the heaven and the earth is a journey of five hundred years."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ﴿and raised couches﴾: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, indeed their height. . ." Then he mentioned the like of it.

And His words: ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production. So We made them virgins, loving﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed We created them with a creation, We brought them into being. Abu ʿUbaydah said: By this is meant the ḥūr ʿīn (wide-eyed maidens) whom He mentioned before, when He said ﴿and wide-eyed maidens like hidden pearls, a reward for what they used to do﴾ and ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾. Al-Akhfash said: He concealed them (in the pronoun) and did not mention them before that.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said concerning this.

And His words: ﴿ʿurub﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So We made them virgins, glancing coquettishly (ghanijāt), loving toward their husbands, graceful in their conjugal relations. It is a plural; its singular is ʿarūb, just as the singular of rusul is rasūl and the singular of qutūf is qatūf. From this is the verse of Labid:

"And in the litters is an ʿarūb, not vulgar, with full hips, whose glance is dazzled by her."

[[This verse is by the poet Labid; Abu ʿUbaydah attributes it to him in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 175b), reciting it at His words "ʿurub atrāban", saying: its singular is ʿarūb, meaning the good in marital devotion (affection toward the husband). Labid: "And in the litters..." the verse. In the original: al-Jazūʿ, which is an error by the copyist. In al-Qurtubi (17:211): al-Khibāʾ, and there is no harm in it. The verse's version in Fath al-Qadir of al-Shawkani (5:149): "Rayya al-rawadif yu'shi ḍawuʾhā al-basara."]]

It means that they are of equal age, of one age; its singular is tirb, as one says: shabah and ashbāh.

Like what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation have said:

Mention of those who said that:

ʿAli ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Rabiʿah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Sabur, from ʿAtiyyah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: al-atrāb: the equal ones.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, His words ﴿atrāban﴾, he said: likenesses.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah ﴿atrāban﴾, meaning: one age.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to me, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, similarly.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: concerning His words ﴿atrāban﴾, he said: al-atrāb: the equal ones.

* *

And His words: ﴿for the companions of the right hand﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We produced these whose description of virgins He has stated, for those who will be taken on the right side (dhāt al-yamīn) from the place of reckoning to Paradise.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 56, verses 32–38:

The explanation of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And fruit in abundance, neither cut off nor forbidden, and raised couches, indeed We have produced them with a special production, and made them virgins, loving (ʿurub), equal in age, for the companions of the right hand.﴾

He says, ﴿And fruit in abundance, neither cut off nor forbidden﴾: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: therein is ﴿fruit in abundance﴾, none of which is cut off from them at any time they desire it, as the fruits of summer are cut off in winter in this world, and none of which is forbidden to them, nor does thorn on its trees or its distance from them come between them and it, as the fruits of this world are withheld from many who desire them, either by their distance on the tree from them or by the thorns on its branches. Rather, when one of them desires it, it falls into his mouth or draws near to him until he takes it with his hand.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said concerning this.

We have already mentioned the narrations on this before, and we will mention some others from them:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, saying: Qatadah narrated to us, concerning His words, ﴿neither cut off nor forbidden﴾, he said: Neither thorn nor distance prevents him from it.

* *

And His words: ﴿and raised couches﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: For them therein are raised couches, long, one above another, as one says: a raised (marfuʿ) building.

Like what has been said:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Rushdin ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn al-Harith, from Darraj Abu al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His words ﴿and raised couches﴾, he said: "Indeed their height is like what is between the heaven and the earth, and what is between the heaven and the earth is a journey of five hundred years."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Saʿid, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ﴿and raised couches﴾: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, indeed their height. . ." Then he mentioned the like of it.

* *

And His words: ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production. So We made them virgins, loving﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed We created them with a creation, We brought them into being. Abu ʿUbaydah said: By this is meant the ḥūr ʿīn (wide-eyed maidens) whom He mentioned before, when He said ﴿and wide-eyed maidens like hidden pearls, a reward for what they used to do﴾ and ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾. Al-Akhfash said: He concealed them (in the pronoun) and did not mention them before that.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾, he said: We created them as a creation.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Shaybān, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Yazid ibn Murrah, from Salamah ibn Yazid, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning this verse, ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾, he said: "Of the previously married and the virgins."

* *

And His words: ﴿So We made them virgins﴾

He says: We made them virgins, maidens, after they had been (old women).[[Perhaps he omitted the predicate of "kunna" relying on its explicit mention in the following hadith; i.e., after they had been old women.]]

As:

Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mahran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Musa ibn ʿUbaydah, from Yazid ibn Aban al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾, he said: "Old women who were in this world blear-eyed and with discharge from the eyes."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mahran narrated to us, from Musa ibn ʿUbaydah, from Yazid ibn Aban al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed We have produced them with a special production", he said: He produced old women who were in this world blear-eyed and with discharge from the eyes.

ʿUmar ibn Ismaʿil ibn Mujalid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Rabiʿah al-Kilabi narrated to us, from Musa ibn ʿUbaydah al-Rabadhi, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, concerning His words ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾, he said: "Among them are the old women who were in this world blear-eyed and with discharge from the eyes."

Sawwar ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Dawud narrated to us, from Musa ibn ʿUbaydah al-Rabadhi, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His words ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾, he said: "They are those who were in this world old women, blear-eyed and with discharge from the eyes."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir narrated to us, from his father, from Qatadah, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, concerning His words ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production. So We made them virgins﴾, he said: They are the decrepit, blear-eyed old women.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, saying: Qatadah narrated to us, concerning His words ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production. So We made them virgins﴾, he said: Among them are the decrepit, trembling old women, whom Allah produced in this creation.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production﴾. Qatadah said: Safwan ibn Muhriz used to say: Among them are the decrepit trembling old women, whom Allah transformed as you hear.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: His words ﴿virgins﴾ mean: maidens.

Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Sadafi al-Dimyati narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi Karimah, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Umm Salamah, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, that she said: I said, O Messenger of Allah, inform me about the saying of Allah ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production. So We made them virgins, loving, equal in age, for the companions of the right hand﴾. He said: "They are those who were taken in this world as old women, blear-eyed, white-haired; Allah created them after old age and made them maidens."

Abu ʿUbayd al-Wassabi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayr narrated to us, saying: Thabit ibn ʿAjlan narrated to us, saying: I heard Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrate from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words ﴿Indeed We have produced them with a special production. So We made them virgins, loving, equal in age﴾, he said: They are of the children of Adam; your women in this world, Allah produces them as virgins, maidens, loving.

* *

And His words: ﴿ʿurub﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So We made them virgins, glancing coquettishly (ghanijāt), loving toward their husbands, graceful in their conjugal relations. It is a plural; its singular is ʿarūb, just as the singular of rusul is rasūl and the singular of qutūf is qatūf. From this is the verse of Labid:

"And in the litters is an ʿarūb, not vulgar, with full hips, whose glance is dazzled by her."

[[This verse is by the poet Labid; Abu ʿUbaydah attributes it to him in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 175b), reciting it at His words "ʿurub atrāban", saying: its singular is ʿarūb, meaning the good in marital devotion (affection toward the husband). Labid: "And in the litters..." the verse. In the original: al-Jazūʿ, which is an error by the copyist. In al-Qurtubi (17:211): al-Khibāʾ, and there is no harm in it. The verse's version in Fath al-Qadir of al-Shawkani (5:149): "Rayya al-rawadif yu'shi ḍawuʾhā al-basara."]]

Like what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation have said:

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ismaʿil ibn Abban and Ismaʿil ibn Subayh narrated to us, from Abu Idris, from Thawr ibn Zayd, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿ʿurub atrāban﴾, he said: al-Malaqah.

ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His words ﴿ʿurub﴾, he says: ʿawashiq (passionately loving).

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: al-ʿurub are the ones who are coquettish and affectionate toward their husbands.

Sulayman ibn ʿUbayd Allah al-Ghaylani narrated to me, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Qurrah informed us, from al-Hasan, who said: al-ʿurub: the one who loves passionately.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Simak, from ʿIkrimah, that he said concerning this verse, ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: al-ʿurub: the coquettish ones (al-maghnūjah).

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Simak ibn ʿIkrimah, who said: They are the coquettish ones (al-maghnūjah).

Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, saying: ʿUmarah ibn Abi Hafsah narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, concerning His words ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: coquettish (ghinjāt).

ʿAli ibn al-Hasan al-Azdi narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq al-Taymi, from Salih ibn Hayyan, from Abu Buraydah ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: al-shaklah in the dialect of Makkah, and al-ghinjah in the dialect of Madinah.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: I heard Ibrahim al-Taymi, i.e., Ibn al-Zabarqan, from Salih ibn Hayyan, from Abu Yazid, with similar.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from ʿUthman ibn Bashshar, from Tamim ibn Hadhlam, concerning His words ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: the good conjugal relations of the woman.

Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from ʿUthman ibn Bashshar, from Tamim ibn Hadhlam, concerning ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: al-ʿaribah: the one good in conjugal relations. He said: The Arabs used to say of a woman when she was good in conjugal relations: "Indeed she is ʿarībah."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Usamah ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: good in speech.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, who said: ʿawashiq.

He said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Shareek, from Khusayf, from Mujahid and ʿIkrimah, similarly.

He said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Husayn, from Mujahid concerning ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: the ʿurub are the affectionate ones.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: the ʿurub: the ʿawashiq.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salim al-Aftas, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, similarly.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ghalib Abu al-Hudhayl, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: the ʿurub are those who desire their husbands.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from al-Mubarak ibn Fudalah, from al-Hasan, who said: those who desire their husbands.

He said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: ʿUthman ibn al-Aswad informed us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUbayd Allah, who said: the ʿurub: she who desires her husband.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from ʿUthman ibn al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: the ʿarībah: she who desires her husband. Do you not see that a man says of a she-camel: "Indeed she is ʿarībah"?

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: ʿushshaq (passionately loving) toward their husbands.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, His words ﴿ʿurub atrāban﴾, he says: ʿushshaq toward their husbands, loving their husbands with intense love.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: al-ʿurub: those who show affection.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿ʿurub atrāban﴾, he said: affectionate toward their husbands.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: al-ʿurub: good in speech.

Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, saying: al-Awza'i was asked about ﴿ʿurub﴾, he said: I heard Yahya say: they are the ʿawashiq.

Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Sadafi al-Dimyati narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Hashim, from Abu Karimah, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from al-Hasan, from his mother, from Umm Salamah, who said: I said, O Messenger of Allah, inform me about His words ﴿ʿurub atrāban﴾. He said: "ʿurub, passionately loving, affectionate; atrāban, of one age."

Muhammad ibn Hafs Abu ʿUbayd al-Wassabi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayr narrated to us, saying: Thabit ibn ʿAjlan narrated to us, saying: I heard Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrate from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿ʿurub﴾, and al-ʿarab: the longing (al-shawq).

The reciters differed in the reading of this. Some reciters of Madinah and some reciters of Kufa read ʿurubā with a damma on the ʿayn and the rāʾ. Some reciters of Kufa and Basra read ﴿wa-ʿurubā﴾ with a damma on the ʿayn and a light rāʾ, and this is the dialect of Tamim and Bakr. The damma in both instances is the more correct of the two readings, for the reason I have mentioned, that it is the plural of ʿarūb; and when fa'ūl, fa'īl or fi'āl is pluralized, it is pluralized as fu'ul with a damma on the fāʾ and ʿayn, whether masculine or feminine. Lightening the ʿayn is permissible, though what I have mentioned is the more eloquent form of the lightened reading.

It means that they are of equal age, of one age; its singular is tirb, as one says: shabah and ashbāh.
