And His words: ﴿for the companions of the right hand﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We produced these whose description of virgins He has stated, for those who will be taken on the right side (dhāt al-yamīn) from the place of reckoning to Paradise.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 56, verses 39–46:

On the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿A multitude from the earlier peoples, and a multitude from the later ones, and the companions of the left hand — what of the companions of the left hand?﴾ Hmm, let me restate precisely below.

Translation of the verses: ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones (39), and a multitude of the later ones (40), and the companions of the left (41), what are the companions of the left? (41) In scorching wind and boiling water (42), and in the shade of black smoke (43), neither cool nor pleasant (44). Indeed they were before that affluent (45), and they used to persist in the great violation (46).﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those who have this honour whose attributes He described in these verses are two multitudes, that is two groups, two nations and two companies: ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones﴾, meaning a group of those who passed before the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And a multitude of the later ones﴾, He says: and a group of the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ). This is what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of the narrations to that effect:

• Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, he said: al-Hasan said: ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones﴾ — from the nations — ﴿and a multitude of the later ones﴾ — the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ).

• Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones﴾, he said: a nation.

• Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, he said: Qatadah related to us, he said: al-Hasan related to us, from the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "We talked in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night until we became lengthy in the discussion, then we returned to our families. When we woke in the morning we went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The prophets were displayed to me last night with their followers from their nations. A prophet would come with a multitude of his nation, and a prophet would come with a band of his nation, and a prophet would come with a small group of his nation, and a prophet would come with one man of his nation, and a prophet would come with no one of his nation at all. Then there came to me Musa ibn 'Imran in a great host of the Children of Israel. When I saw them, they amazed me, and I said: O Lord, who are these? He said: This is your brother Musa ibn 'Imran and those with him from the Children of Israel. I said: O Lord, then where is my nation? It was said: Look to your right, and there, the mountain-slopes of Makkah were filled with the faces of men. I said: Who are these? It was said: These are your nation. It was said: Are you content? I said: My Lord, I am content, my Lord, I am content. It was said: Look to your left, and there the horizon was filled with the faces of men. I said: O Lord, who are these? It was said: These are your nation. It was said: Are you content? I said: I am content, my Lord, I am content. It was said: With these there are seventy thousand of your nation who will enter Paradise without reckoning.' He said: Then 'Ukkashah ibn Mihsan, a man of the Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah, stood up and said: O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them. He said: O Allah, make him one of them. Then another man stood up and said: O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them. He said: 'Ukkashah has preceded you with it. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: May my father and mother be ransom for you. If you are able to be among the seventy, then be so; if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the mountain-slopes; and if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the horizon, for I have seen people there (in the horizon) who are crowding and surging, many of them, or he said: rushing upon one another.' He said: So the believers turned back, or he said: So we turned back from these seventy, and it became their matter that they said: We consider them to be people who were born in Islam and continued to act upon it until they died upon it. This account reached the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'It is not so, rather they are those who do not seek incantation (istirqa'), nor cauterization (ikhtiwa'), nor divination by omens (tatayyur), and upon their Lord they rely.'" It is mentioned that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said that day: "I truly hope that those who follow me from my nation will be a quarter of the people of Paradise," so we exclaimed Allahu akbar, then he said: "I truly hope that you will be half," so we exclaimed Allahu akbar, then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones, and a multitude of the later ones﴾.

• Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Bishr al-Bajali related to us, from al-Hakam ibn 'Abd al-Malik, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "We talked one night in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until we became lengthy or nearly so," then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: "...and there the mountain-slopes of Makkah were blocked with the faces of men." And he also said: "I saw there people rushing upon one another greatly." He said: We said: Who are these seventy thousand? Our opinion agreed that they were people born in Islam and who die upon it. He said: We mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "No, rather they are a people who do not cauterize." And he also said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I truly hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise," so his companions exclaimed Allahu akbar; then he said: "I truly hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise," so his companions exclaimed Allahu akbar; then he said: "I truly hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise," then he recited ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones, and a multitude of the later ones﴾.

• Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Awf, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith, he said: "They are all in Paradise."

• Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, that it reached him that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Are you content to be a quarter of the people of Paradise? They said: Yes. He said: Are you content to be a third of the people of Paradise? They said: Yes. The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 56, verses 39–46:

On the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿A multitude from the earlier peoples, and a multitude from the later ones, and the companions of the left hand — what of the companions of the left hand?﴾ Hmm, let me restate precisely below.

Translation of the verses: ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones (39), and a multitude of the later ones (40), and the companions of the left (41), what are the companions of the left? (41) In scorching wind and boiling water (42), and in the shade of black smoke (43), neither cool nor pleasant (44). Indeed they were before that affluent (45), and they used to persist in the great violation (46).﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those who have this honour whose attributes He described in these verses are two multitudes, that is two groups, two nations and two companies: ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones﴾, meaning a group of those who passed before the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And a multitude of the later ones﴾, He says: and a group of the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ). This is what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of the narrations to that effect:

• Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, he said: al-Hasan said: ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones﴾ — from the nations — ﴿and a multitude of the later ones﴾ — the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ).

• Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones﴾, he said: a nation.

• Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, he said: Qatadah related to us, he said: al-Hasan related to us, from the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "We talked in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night until we became lengthy in the discussion, then we returned to our families. When we woke in the morning we went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The prophets were displayed to me last night with their followers from their nations. A prophet would come with a multitude of his nation, and a prophet would come with a band of his nation, and a prophet would come with a small group of his nation, and a prophet would come with one man of his nation, and a prophet would come with no one of his nation at all. Then there came to me Musa ibn 'Imran in a great host of the Children of Israel. When I saw them, they amazed me, and I said: O Lord, who are these? He said: This is your brother Musa ibn 'Imran and those with him from the Children of Israel. I said: O Lord, then where is my nation? It was said: Look to your right, and there, the mountain-slopes of Makkah were filled with the faces of men. I said: Who are these? It was said: These are your nation. It was said: Are you content? I said: My Lord, I am content, my Lord, I am content. It was said: Look to your left, and there the horizon was filled with the faces of men. I said: O Lord, who are these? It was said: These are your nation. It was said: Are you content? I said: I am content, my Lord, I am content. It was said: With these there are seventy thousand of your nation who will enter Paradise without reckoning.' He said: Then 'Ukkashah ibn Mihsan, a man of the Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah, stood up and said: O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them. He said: O Allah, make him one of them. Then another man stood up and said: O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them. He said: 'Ukkashah has preceded you with it. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: May my father and mother be ransom for you. If you are able to be among the seventy, then be so; if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the mountain-slopes; and if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the horizon, for I have seen people there (in the horizon) who are crowding and surging, many of them, or he said: rushing upon one another.' He said: So the believers turned back, or he said: So we turned back from these seventy, and it became their matter that they said: We consider them to be people who were born in Islam and continued to act upon it until they died upon it. This account reached the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'It is not so, rather they are those who do not seek incantation (istirqa'), nor cauterization (ikhtiwa'), nor divination by omens (tatayyur), and upon their Lord they rely.'" It is mentioned that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said that day: "I truly hope that those who follow me from my nation will be a quarter of the people of Paradise," so we exclaimed Allahu akbar, then he said: "I truly hope that you will be half," so we exclaimed Allahu akbar, then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones, and a multitude of the later ones﴾.

And he also said: "I saw there people rushing upon one another greatly." He said: We said: Who are these seventy thousand? Our opinion agreed that they were people born in Islam and who die upon it. He said: We mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "No, rather they are a people who do not cauterize." And he also said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I truly hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise," so his companions exclaimed Allahu akbar; then he said: "I truly hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise," so his companions exclaimed Allahu akbar; then he said: "I truly hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise," then he recited ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones, and a multitude of the later ones﴾.

Indeed they were before that affluent (45), and they used to persist in the great violation (46).﴾

When we woke in the morning we went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The prophets were displayed to me last night with their followers from their nations. A prophet would come with a multitude of his nation, and a prophet would come with a band of his nation, and a prophet would come with a small group of his nation, and a prophet would come with one man of his nation, and a prophet would come with no one of his nation at all. He said: This is your brother Musa ibn 'Imran and those with him from the Children of Israel. I said: O Lord, then where is my nation? I said: My Lord, I am content, my Lord, I am content. It was said: Look to your left, and there the horizon was filled with the faces of men. I said: O Lord, who are these? It was said: These are your nation. It was said: Are you content? I said: I am content, my Lord, I am content. Then another man stood up and said: O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them. He said: 'Ukkashah has preceded you with it. And he also said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I truly hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise," so his companions exclaimed Allahu akbar; then he said: "I truly hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise," so his companions exclaimed Allahu akbar; then he said: "I truly hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise," then he recited ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones, and a multitude of the later ones﴾.

(41) In scorching wind and boiling water (42), and in the shade of black smoke (43), neither cool nor pleasant (44). Indeed they were before that affluent (45), and they used to persist in the great violation (46).﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those who have this honour whose attributes He described in these verses are two multitudes, that is two groups, two nations and two companies: ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones﴾, meaning a group of those who passed before the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And a multitude of the later ones﴾, He says: and a group of the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ). This is what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

When we woke in the morning we went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The prophets were displayed to me last night with their followers from their nations. A prophet would come with a multitude of his nation, and a prophet would come with a band of his nation, and a prophet would come with a small group of his nation, and a prophet would come with one man of his nation, and a prophet would come with no one of his nation at all. Then there came to me Musa ibn 'Imran in a great host of the Children of Israel. When I saw them, they amazed me, and I said: O Lord, who are these? He said: This is your brother Musa ibn 'Imran and those with him from the Children of Israel. I said: O Lord, then where is my nation? It was said: Look to your right, and there, the mountain-slopes of Makkah were filled with the faces of men. I said: Who are these? It was said: These are your nation. It was said: Are you content? I said: My Lord, I am content, my Lord, I am content. It was said: Look to your left, and there the horizon was filled with the faces of men. I said: O Lord, who are these? It was said: These are your nation. It was said: Are you content? I said: I am content, my Lord, I am content. He said: Then 'Ukkashah ibn Mihsan, a man of the Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah, stood up and said: O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them. He said: O Allah, make him one of them. Then another man stood up and said: O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them. He said: 'Ukkashah has preceded you with it. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: May my father and mother be ransom for you. If you are able to be among the seventy, then be so; if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the mountain-slopes; and if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the horizon, for I have seen people there (in the horizon) who are crowding and surging, many of them, or he said: rushing upon one another.' He said: So the believers turned back, or he said: So we turned back from these seventy, and it became their matter that they said: We consider them to be people who were born in Islam and continued to act upon it until they died upon it. This account reached the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'It is not so, rather they are those who do not seek incantation (istirqa'), nor cauterization (ikhtiwa'), nor divination by omens (tatayyur), and upon their Lord they rely.'" It was said: Look to your right, and there, the mountain-slopes of Makkah were filled with the faces of men. I said: Who are these? It was said: These are your nation. It was said: Are you content? I said: My Lord, I am content, my Lord, I am content. It was said: Look to your left, and there the horizon was filled with the faces of men. I said: O Lord, who are these? It was said: These are your nation. It was said: Are you content? I said: I am content, my Lord, I am content. It was said: With these there are seventy thousand of your nation who will enter Paradise without reckoning.' He said: Then 'Ukkashah ibn Mihsan, a man of the Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah, stood up and said: O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them. He said: O Allah, make him one of them. Then another man stood up and said: O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them. He said: 'Ukkashah has preceded you with it. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: May my father and mother be ransom for you. If you are able to be among the seventy, then be so; if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the mountain-slopes; and if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the horizon, for I have seen people there (in the horizon) who are crowding and surging, many of them, or he said: rushing upon one another.' He said: So the believers turned back, or he said: So we turned back from these seventy, and it became their matter that they said: We consider them to be people who were born in Islam and continued to act upon it until they died upon it. This account reached the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'It is not so, rather they are those who do not seek incantation (istirqa'), nor cauterization (ikhtiwa'), nor divination by omens (tatayyur), and upon their Lord they rely.'" It is mentioned that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said that day: "I truly hope that those who follow me from my nation will be a quarter of the people of Paradise," so we exclaimed Allahu akbar, then he said: "I truly hope that you will be half," so we exclaimed Allahu akbar, then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones, and a multitude of the later ones﴾.

And he also said: "I saw there people rushing upon one another greatly." He said: We said: Who are these seventy thousand? Our opinion agreed that they were people born in Islam and who die upon it. He said: We mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "No, rather they are a people who do not cauterize." And he also said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I truly hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise," so his companions exclaimed Allahu akbar; then he said: "I truly hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise," so his companions exclaimed Allahu akbar; then he said: "I truly hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise," then he recited ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones, and a multitude of the later ones﴾.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 56, verses 39–46:

On the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿A multitude from the earlier peoples, and a multitude from the later ones, and the companions of the left hand — what of the companions of the left hand?﴾ Hmm, let me restate precisely below.

Translation of the verses: ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones (39), and a multitude of the later ones (40), and the companions of the left (41), what are the companions of the left? (41) In scorching wind and boiling water (42), and in the shade of black smoke (43), neither cool nor pleasant (44). Indeed they were before that affluent (45), and they used to persist in the great violation (46).﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those who have this honour whose attributes He described in these verses are two multitudes, that is two groups, two nations and two companies: ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones﴾, meaning a group of those who passed before the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And a multitude of the later ones﴾, He says: and a group of the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ). This is what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

When we woke in the morning we went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The prophets were displayed to me last night with their followers from their nations. A prophet would come with a multitude of his nation, and a prophet would come with a band of his nation, and a prophet would come with a small group of his nation, and a prophet would come with one man of his nation, and a prophet would come with no one of his nation at all. The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 56, verses 39–46:

On the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿A multitude from the earlier peoples, and a multitude from the later ones, and the companions of the left hand — what of the companions of the left hand?﴾ Hmm, let me restate precisely below.

Translation of the verses: ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones (39), and a multitude of the later ones (40), and the companions of the left (41), what are the companions of the left? (41) In scorching wind and boiling water (42), and in the shade of black smoke (43), neither cool nor pleasant (44). Indeed they were before that affluent (45), and they used to persist in the great violation (46).﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those who have this honour whose attributes He described in these verses are two multitudes, that is two groups, two nations and two companies: ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones﴾, meaning a group of those who passed before the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And a multitude of the later ones﴾, He says: and a group of the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ). This is what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of the narrations to that effect:

• Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, he said: al-Hasan said: ﴿A multitude of the earlier ones﴾ — from the nations — ﴿and a multitude of the later ones﴾ — the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ).

When we woke in the morning we went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The prophets were displayed to me last night with their followers from their nations. A prophet would come with a multitude of his nation, and a prophet would come with a band of his nation, and a prophet would come with a small group of his nation, and a prophet would come with one man of his nation, and a prophet would come with no one of his nation at all. Then there came to me Musa ibn 'Imran in a great host of the Children of Israel. When I saw them, they amazed me, and I said: O Lord, who are these? He said: This is your brother Musa ibn 'Imran and those with him from the Children of Israel. I said: O Lord, then where is my nation? It was said: Look to your right, and there, the mountain-slopes of Makkah were filled with the faces of men. I said: Who are these? It was said: These are your nation. It was said: Are you content? I said: My Lord, I am content, my Lord, I am content. It was said: Look to your left, and there the horizon was filled with the faces of men. I said: O Lord, who are these? It was said: These are your nation. It was said: Are you content? I said: I am content, my Lord, I am content. It was said: With these there are seventy thousand of your nation who will enter Paradise without reckoning.' He said: Then 'Ukkashah ibn Mihsan, a man of the Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah, stood up and said: O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them. He said: O Allah, make him one of them. Then another man stood up and said: O Prophet of Allah, ask your Lord to make me one of them. He said: 'Ukkashah has preceded you with it. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: May my father and mother be ransom for you. If you are able to be among the seventy, then be so; if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the mountain-slopes; and if you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the horizon, for I have seen people there (in the horizon) who are crowding and surging, many of them, or he said: rushing upon one another.' He said: So the believers turned back, or he said: So we turned back from these seventy, and it became their matter that they said: We consider them to be people who were born in Islam and continued to act upon it until they died upon it. **The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Then indeed you, O you who go astray, who deny,﴾ ﴿shall surely eat from a tree of zaqqum,﴾ ﴿and fill your bellies with it,﴾**

God, exalted is His remembrance, says to the companions of the left: Then indeed you, O you who have strayed from the path of guidance and who deny the threat and promise of God, shall surely eat from a tree of zaqqum.

* *

As for His words, ﴿and fill your bellies with it﴾:

He says: you will fill your bellies with the zaqqum tree.

The grammarians of Arabic (ahl al-'Arabiyya, the scholars of the Arabic language) differed over the reason for the feminine form in His words ﴿with it﴾ (فَمَالِئُونَ مِنْهَا), where the reference is to the tree (الشجر). The verse also says ﴿and drink on top of it﴾ (فَشَارِبُونَ عَلَيْهِ), with the masculine pronoun. The reason is that the word shajar (شجر, "tree") may be treated as feminine or masculine. The feminine was used here because shajarah (شجرة, "a tree"), the singular form, can denote the whole category. The Arabs say: "There grew before us a bitter shajarah and a poor herb," and they mean the whole class. Some of the Kufan grammarians said that the phrase ﴿eat from a tree of zaqqum﴾ (لآكِلُونَ مِنْ شَجَرٍ مِنْ زَقُّومٍ) and in the reading of 'Abd Allah (ﷺ?) ﴿eat from a tree of zaqqum﴾ with shajarah (شجرة) in the singular are the same in meaning, since shajar and shajarah have one meaning. This is because when you say akhadtu min al-shā' (أخذت من الشاء, "I took from the sheep"), whether you intend one or more than one, it is permissible. Then He said ﴿with it﴾ (مِنْهَا), meaning from the tree (الشجرة). Had He said منه (minhu, "from it," masculine) when the word shajar was not mentioned, it would have been correct, referring to shajar in the sense of the masculine pronoun, while treating shajar as feminine, so that minhā would be a pronoun referring to shajar. Shajar can be both feminine and masculine, like tamr (تمر, "dates"), which can be both feminine and masculine.

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is the second view, namely that His words ﴿with it﴾ (فَمَالِئُونَ مِنْهَا) refer to shajar, and it is feminine according to the meaning, while His words ﴿on top of it﴾ (فَشَارِبُونَ عَلَيْهِ) are masculine according to the wording of shajar.

His, may He be exalted and remembered, says: this which I have described to you, O people, that these deniers who went astray eat from the tree of zaqqum and drink on top of it from the scalding water, is their hospitality which their Lord bestows upon them on the Day of Judgment, meaning: the Day on which God requites His servants.

* *

As for His saying ﴿We created you, so why do you not believe?﴾:

His, may He be exalted and remembered, says to the disbelievers of Quraysh and to those who deny the Resurrection: We created you, O people, when you were nothing, and brought you into existence as humans. So why do you not believe in the One who did this to you, in His saying to you that He will resurrect you after your death and your decay in your graves, as He made you before your death?

The Interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Have you considered that which you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creator?﴾ [56:58-59]

Almighty God says to these deniers of the Resurrection: Have you considered, you deniers, the power of God to bring you back to life after your death, namely the drops of seed that you emit into the wombs of your women? Is it you who create them, or are We the Creator?

Almighty God says: We have decreed death among you, O people, so We hasten it for some and delay it for others until a specified term.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 56, verses 62–64:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you have certainly known the first creation, so why do you not remember?﴾ (62) ﴿Have you considered that which you plant?﴾ (63) ﴿Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾ (64)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: And you have certainly known the first creation, O people, the initiation that We initiated for you, when you were not anything before that.

Those who interpret the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿the first creation﴾, he said: when you were not anything.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿And you have certainly known the first creation﴾, meaning the creation of Adam. You will not ask anyone among the creation but that he will inform you that God created Adam from clay.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿And you have certainly known the first creation﴾, he said: it is the creation of Adam.

* Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harasi narrated to me, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu 'Imran al-Jawni recite this verse: ﴿And you have certainly known the first creation﴾, he said: it is the creation of Adam.

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Why then do you not remember, O people, so that you would know that He who originated you in the first creation, when you were not anything, is not incapable of returning you after your death and your annihilation, alive.

* *

As for His words, ﴿and you would be left amazed (tafakkahun)﴾:

The exegetes differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: you would be left wondering at the calamity that befell you in your crop, by its burning and its destruction.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words, ﴿and you would be left amazed (tafakkahun)﴾: he said: you would be astonished.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and you would be left amazed (tafakkahun)﴾: he said: you would be astonished.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and you would be left amazed (tafakkahun)﴾: he said: you would be astonished.

Others said: the meaning of that is: you would be left reproaching one another for your neglect of obedience to your Lord, exalted is His praise, until what befell you of the destruction of your crop reached you.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, from Yazid, from Ikrimah, regarding His words, ﴿and you would be left amazed (tafakkahun)﴾: he says: you would be reproaching one another.

- He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Simak ibn Harb al-Bakri, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿and you would be left amazed (tafakkahun)﴾: he said: you would be reproaching one another.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: you would be left regretting what had passed from you of disobedience to God, for which He had made His punishment obligatory upon you, until what befell you in your crop reached you.

Those who said this:

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to me, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿and you would be left amazed (tafakkahun)﴾: he said: you would be regretting.

- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, ﴿and you would be left amazed (tafakkahun)﴾: he said: you would be regretting.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: you would be left wondering.

Those who said this:

- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, ﴿and you would be left amazed (tafakkahun)﴾: he said: you would be wondering when what was done to your tillage was done to it, and he recited the words of God, mighty and majestic, ﴿Indeed, we are laden with debt, * Rather, we are deprived﴾, and he recited the words of God, ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting (fakihin)﴾, and he said: these were in luxury. And he recited the words of God, exalted is His praise, ﴿So We expelled them from gardens and springs﴾ ... to His words: ﴿They were therein fruit-eaters (fakihin)﴾.

The most correct of these sayings in interpretation is the saying of the one who said: the meaning of ﴿fazaltum﴾ is: you would remain wondering at what befell your crop. Its root is from tafakkuh in speech, when a man relates a story to another man, marveling at it and being diverted by it; so likewise is this. The sense of the speech is: you would remain wondering, making one another marvel at what has befallen you.

* *

As for His words, ﴿Indeed, we are laden with debt (mughramun)﴾:

The exegetes differed concerning its meaning. Some of them said: it means: we are seized with (mawlaʿun) an affliction.

Those who said this:

- Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi related to me, he said: Yazid ibn al-Habbab related to us, he said: al-Husayn ibn Waqid informed me, he said: Yazid al-Nahwi related to me, from Ikrimah, regarding the words of God, exalted is His remembrance, ﴿Indeed, we are laden with debt﴾: he said: we are seized with affliction.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, he said: Mujahid said regarding His words, ﴿Indeed, we are laden with debt﴾: i.e., seized with affliction.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: we are being punished.

Those who said this:

- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Indeed, we are laden with debt﴾: i.e., being punished.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: we are cast into evil.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿Indeed, we are laden with debt﴾: he said: cast into evil.

The most correct of these sayings in interpretation is the saying of the one who said: its meaning is: we are being punished. That is because al-gharam (debt/penalty) among the Arabs means punishment, and from it is the verse of al-A'sha:

"If he punishes, it will be a gharam; and if he gives abundantly, he does not care."

He means by His words, "yakun gharaman": "yakun 'adhaban" (it will be a punishment). In the speech there is an omitted element which the meaning of the speech makes evident, namely: "you would be left jesting, [saying]" Indeed, we are laden with debt, so "taqulun" (you say) has been omitted from the speech for what we have described.

* *

As for His words, ﴿Rather, we are deprived (mahrumun)﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, means by this that they would say: our crop was not destroyed and we were struck by it because of "Indeed, we are laden with debt," but rather we are a people deprived, meaning: they are not favored, having no good fortune.

The exegetes have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿Rather, we are deprived﴾: he said: we were made to suffer loss and so were deprived.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words, ﴿Rather, we are deprived﴾: he said: i.e., those who suffer losses (mihrafun).

The sense of the speech is: you would remain wondering, making one another marvel at what has befallen you.

* *

As for His words, ﴿Indeed, we are laden with debt (mughramun)﴾:

The exegetes differed concerning its meaning. Some of them said: it means: we are seized with (mawlaʿun) an affliction.

Those who said this:

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: we are being punished.

Those who said this:

He means by His words, "yakun gharaman": "yakun 'adhaban" (it will be a punishment). The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Have you considered the water which you drink? Is it you who brought it down from the cloud, or are We the Sender?  If We willed, We could make it salty; so why do you not give thanks?﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Have you considered, O people, the water that you drink? Is it you who sent it down from the clouds above you to the bottom of the earth, or are We the ones who send it down for you?

* * *

His, the Exalted's, saying means: If We willed, We could make that water which We sent down to you from the muzn salty, and that is ajaj; and ajaj of water is that whose saltiness has become intense. The meaning: If We willed, We would do that to it, and you would not benefit from it for drinking, planting, or sowing.

* * *

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Why do you not give thanks to your Lord for granting you the sweet water for your drinking and your benefits and the well-being of your livelihoods, and for not making it ajaj so that you could not benefit from it?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 56, verses 71–73:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have you considered the fire which you kindle? (71) Is it you who produced its tree, or are We the producer? (72) We have made it a reminder and a provision for the travelers (al-muqwin).﴾ (73)

His saying, Exalted is His remembrance: Have you considered, O people, the fire that you extract from your flint? ﴿Is it you who produced its tree?﴾ That is, did you create its tree and invent its origin? ﴿Or are We the producer?﴾ That is, did We invent that and bring it into being?

* *

And His saying: ﴿We have made it a reminder﴾

That is: We made the fire a reminder for you, by which you remember the fire of Hell, so that you may take heed and be admonished by it.

This is also the view of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil), in line with what we have said.

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿a reminder﴾, he said: a reminder of the Great Fire.

⁕ Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Have you considered the fire which you kindle? * Is it you who produced its tree, or are We the producer? * We have made it a reminder﴾, that it is for the Great Fire.

It has been mentioned to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This fire of yours which you kindle is a part of seventy parts of the fire of Hell." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed it would suffice." He said: "It has been struck with water twice or two times, so that the children of Adam may benefit from it and draw near to it."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿a reminder﴾, he said: for the Great Fire that is in the Hereafter.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and a provision for the travelers (al-muqwin)﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of al-muqwin. Some of them said: they are the travelers.

Those who said this:

⁕ 'Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿for the muqwin﴾, he said: for the travelers.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and a provision for the muqwin﴾, he said: it means the travelers.

⁕ Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿and a provision for the muqwin﴾, he said: for the one who is mursil (one who has run out of provisions), the traveler.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿for the muqwin﴾, he said: for the travelers.

⁕ It was related to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿and a provision for the muqwin﴾, he said: for the travelers.

Others said: By al-muqwin is meant those who benefit from it (al-mustamti'in biha).

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿and a provision for the muqwin﴾, for those who benefit from it, all of mankind.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid regarding ﴿and a provision for the muqwin﴾, for those who benefit from it, the traveler and the resident.

⁕ Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Habib al-Shahid related to me, he said: 'Attab ibn Bashir related to us, from Khusayf regarding His saying: ﴿and a provision for the muqwin﴾, he said: for creation.

Others said: Rather, it means: the hungry.

Those who said this:

⁕ Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd, regarding His saying: ﴿and a provision for the muqwin﴾, he said: al-muqwi is the hungry in the speech of the Arabs; they say: "aqwaytu minhu kadhā wa kadhā," meaning: I ate from it such-and-such amount of something.

The most correct of these opinions in my view is the opinion of the one who said: it means the traveler who has no provision with him and nothing of his own, and its root derives from their saying: "aqwat al-dar" when the house became empty of its people and inhabitants, as the poet said:

*aqwā wa aqfara min Nu'min wa ghayyaraha*
*hūju al-riyāh bi-hābī al-turbi mawwār* [[The verse is by al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani from his qasida beginning "'awjū fa-hayyū li-Nu'min dimnat al-dār," being the second verse after the opening. By "aqfara" he means: became empty of its inhabitants.]]

By his saying "aqwā" he means: became empty of its inhabitants. The muqwi may also mean the one with a strong horse, or the one with much wealth, but that is not the meaning in this context.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿a reminder﴾, he said: a reminder of the Great Fire.

⁕ Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿Have you considered the fire which you kindle? * Is it you who produced its tree, or are We the producer? * We have made it a reminder﴾, that it is for the Great Fire.

It has been mentioned to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This fire of yours which you kindle is a part of seventy parts of the fire of Hell." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed it would suffice." He said: "It has been struck with water twice or two times, so that the children of Adam may benefit from it and draw near to it."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿a reminder﴾, he said: for the Great Fire that is in the Hereafter.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and a provision for the travelers (al-muqwin)﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of al-muqwin. Some of them said: they are the travelers.

Those who said this:

⁕ 'Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿for the muqwin﴾, he said: for the travelers.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and a provision for the muqwin﴾, he said: it means the travelers.

⁕ Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿and a provision for the muqwin﴾, he said: for the one who is mursil (one who has run out of provisions), the traveler.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿for the muqwin﴾, he said: for the travelers.

⁕ It was related to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿and a provision for the muqwin﴾, he said: for the travelers.

Others said: By al-muqwin is meant those who benefit from it (al-mustamti'in biha).

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿and a provision for the muqwin﴾, for those who benefit from it, all of mankind.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid regarding ﴿and a provision for the muqwin﴾, for those who benefit from it, the traveler and the resident.

⁕ Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Habib al-Shahid related to me, he said: 'Attab ibn Bashir related to us, from Khusayf regarding His saying: ﴿and a provision for the muqwin﴾, he said: for creation.

Others said: Rather, it means: the hungry.

Those who said this:

⁕ Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd, regarding His saying: ﴿and a provision for the muqwin﴾, he said: al-muqwi is the hungry in the speech of the Arabs; they say: "aqwaytu minhu kadhā wa kadhā," meaning: I ate from it such-and-such amount of something.

The most correct of these opinions in my view is the opinion of the one who said: it means the traveler who has no provision with him and nothing of his own, and its root derives from their saying: "aqwat al-dar" when the house became empty of its people and inhabitants, as the poet said:

*aqwā wa aqfara min Nu'min wa ghayyaraha*
*hūju al-riyāh bi-hābī al-turbi mawwār* [[The verse is by al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani from his qasida beginning "'awjū fa-hayyū li-Nu'min dimnat al-dār," being the second verse after the opening. William Alward of Prussia mentioned it in al-'Iqd al-thamin, p. 269, and considered the poem to be among the spurious poetry attributed to al-Nabigha. The poem has forty-seven verses. The author cited the verse at His saying "and a provision for the muqwin," saying: it means the traveler who has no provision and nothing, and its root is from "aqwat al-dar" when it became empty of its people and inhabitants, as the poem says: "aqwā wa aqfara ... the verse." By "aqfara" he means: became empty of its inhabitants.]]

By his saying "aqwā" he means: became empty of its inhabitants. The muqwi may also mean the one with a strong horse, or the one with much wealth, but that is not the meaning in this context.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 56, verses 74–80:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty (74). So I swear by the positions of the stars (75). And indeed, it is an oath, if you only knew, great (76). Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an (77), in a Book well-protected (78). None touches it except the purified (79). A revelation from the Lord of the worlds (80).﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): So glorify, O Muhammad, with the mention of your Mighty Lord and His naming.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars﴾

The exegetes differed over the interpretation of His saying: ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars﴾. Some of them said: By His saying ﴿So I swear﴾ is meant: I swear.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿So I swear﴾, he said: I swear.

Some of the Arabic grammarians said: The meaning of His saying ﴿So (fa-la)﴾ is: "It is not as you say," and then the oath is begun afterwards, so it is said: "I swear." As for His saying ﴿by the positions of the stars﴾, the exegetes differed over its meaning. Some of them said: Its meaning is: So I swear by the positions of the Qur'an, and they said: The Qur'an was sent down to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in scattered portions (nujum).

Those who said that:

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Qur'an was sent down on the Night of Power (laylat al-qadr) from the highest heaven to the lowest heaven all at once, then it was distributed over the years afterwards. He said: Ibn Abbas recited this verse: ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars﴾, and said: It was sent down in portions.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Yazid, from Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars﴾, he said: God sent down the Qur'an in portions of three verses, four verses and five verses.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, from Ikrimah: The Qur'an was sent down all together, and placed at the positions of the stars, and Jibril would bring the surah, and it was only sent down all together on the Night of Power.

⁕ Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid: ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars﴾, he said: It is the firmly established (muhkam) Qur'an.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars * And indeed, it is an oath, if you only knew, great﴾, he said: the established place of the Book, its beginning and its end.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: So I swear by the falling of the stars.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿by the positions of the stars﴾, he said: in the sky, and it is said their risings and their settings.

⁕ Bishr narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars﴾, meaning: their settings.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: by the stations of the stars.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars﴾, he said: by the stations of the stars.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: by the scattering of the stars at the establishment of the Hour.

Those who said that:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars﴾, he said: al-Hasan said: their being darkened and scattered on the Day of Resurrection.

The most correct of the sayings regarding this, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: So I swear by the settings of the stars and their disappearances in the sky. This is because al-mawaqi' is the plural of mawqi', and mawqi' is a maf'il form from waqa'a yaqa' waqa'an. The most prevalent of its meanings and the most apparent of its interpretations is what we have said regarding it, and for this reason we have said that it is the most fitting of its meanings for it.

The readers differed over the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it as bi-mawqi' in the singular, while the majority of the readers of Madina and Basra and some of the Kufans recited it as bi-mawaqi' in the plural.

The correct view regarding this is that they are two well-known recitations with one meaning, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is an oath, if you only knew, great﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: And indeed this oath which I have sworn is an oath, if you knew what it is and its value, a great oath. It is an inverted (mu'akhkhar) expression whose meaning is the front (taqdim), and it is only: And indeed it is a great oath, if you knew its greatness.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: So I swear by the positions of the stars that this is a noble Qur'an. The pronoun in His saying ﴿indeed, it﴾ refers to the mention of the Qur'an.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿in a Book well-protected﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: It is in a Book preserved with God, which nothing of harm from dust or other than it touches.

The exegetes said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

⁕ Isma'il ibn Musa narrated to me, saying: Sharik informed us, from Hakim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾: the Book which is in the heaven.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿in a Book well-protected﴾: he said: the Qur'an is in His well-protected Book, which nothing of dust or earth touches.

⁕ It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾: They claim that the devils descended with it upon Muhammad, so God informed them that they are not able to do that and cannot manage it; it is not fitting for them to descend with this, and it is veiled from them. And he recited the saying of God: ﴿And it is not fitting for them, nor are they able. Indeed they are removed far from the hearing﴾.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah, meaning al-Ataki, narrated to us, from Jabir ibn Zayd and Abu Nuhayk, regarding His saying ﴿in a Book well-protected﴾: he said: it is a Book in the heaven.

* *

His saying: ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: None touches that well-protected Book except those whom God has purified from sins.

The exegetes differed over those meant by His saying ﴿except the purified﴾. Some of them said: They are the angels.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When God wishes to send down a Book, the scribes (safara) copy it, and none touches it except the purified; he said: meaning the angels.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Abi Rashid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾: he said: the angels who are in the heaven.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Rabi' ibn Abi Rashid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾: he said: the angels.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Rabi' ibn Abi Rashid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾: he said: the angels.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah, meaning al-Ataki, narrated to us, from Jabbar ibn Zayd and Abu Nuhayk, regarding His saying ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾: he says: the angels.

⁕ He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾: he said: the angels.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾: he said: the angels.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Asim, from Abu al-Aliyah, regarding ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾: he said: the angels.

Others said: They are the bearers of the Torah and the Gospel.

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾: he said: the bearers of the Torah and the Gospel.

Others said regarding that: They are those who have been purified from sins, like the angels and the messengers.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Marwan narrated to us, saying: Asim al-Ahwal informed us, from Abu al-Aliyah al-Riyahi, regarding His saying ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾: he said: You are not the people of sins.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾: The angels, the prophets and the messengers to whom it is brought down from God are purified; and the prophets are purified, so Jibril descends with it purified, and the messengers to whom you bring it are purified; that is His saying ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾. The angels, prophets and messengers are from the angels, and the messengers are from the children of Adam; these descend with it purified, and these recite it to the people purified. And he recited the saying of God: ﴿By the hands of scribes, noble and dutiful﴾, and said: By the hands of the angels who count the deeds of people.

Others said: What is meant by that is: None touches it with God except the purified.

Those who said that:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾: that is with the Lord of the worlds; as for with you, the polytheist, the impure, and the hypocrite, the filthy, touch it.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾: he said: None touches it with God except the purified; as for in this world, the Magian impure one and the hypocrite filthy one touch it. And in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: ﴿Only the purified touch it﴾.

The correct view in our opinion regarding this is that God, may His praise be exalted, informed that none touches the well-protected Book except the purified, so He made His information general to the purified, and did not specify some over others. So the angels are among the purified, and the messengers and prophets are among the purified, and everyone who is purified from sins is among those excepted, and by His saying ﴿except the purified﴾ is meant.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿A revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾

He says: This Qur'an is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds, sent down by Him from the well-protected Book.

As:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah al-Ataki narrated to us, from Jabir ibn Zayd and Abu Nuhayk, regarding His saying ﴿A revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾: he said: the Qur'an is from that Book.

As for His saying: ﴿A revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾

He says: This Qur'an is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds, sent down by Him from the well-protected Book.

As:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah al-Ataki narrated to us, from Jabir ibn Zayd and Abu Nuhayk, regarding His saying ﴿A revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾: he said: the Qur'an is from that Book.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He: "Do you then treat this discourse with scorn? And do you make your sustenance [your share] that you deny it? Why then, when it [the soul] reaches the throat, and you at that time are looking on, and We are nearer to it than you, but you do not see."

Exalted is He says: Do you, O people, then soften your speech toward those who deny this Qur'an, of which I have informed you and whose matter I have related to you, out of complicity with them in denying it and disbelieving in it?

The exegetes differed in its interpretation. Some of them said, concerning it, something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of God: "Do you then treat this discourse with scorn?" He said: You wish to collude with them in it, and incline toward them.

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: "Do you then deny this discourse?"

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning his words: "Do you then treat this discourse with scorn?" He said: deniers, not believers.

I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning the words: "You are treating [it] with scorn." He said: deniers.

And His words: "And do you make your sustenance [your share] that you deny it?"

He says: And do you make the thanks for God's provision to you denial? This is like the saying of another poet: "I made my kindness to you into an injury from you to me," meaning: I made the thanks for my kindness, or the reward for my kindness to you, into an injury from you to me.

It has been mentioned from al-Haytham ibn Adi that among the dialect of the Azd Shanu'a is: "what [so-and-so] was provided" meaning "what [so-and-so] thanked."

And according to what we have said concerning this, the people of reflection also said, with some difference among them.

Those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, saying: Abd al-A'la al-Tha'labi related to me, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, may God be pleased with him: "And do you make your sustenance [your share] that you deny it?" He said: your thanks.

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, from Isra'il, from Abd al-A'la al-Tha'labi, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, raising it [to the Prophet]: "And do you make your sustenance [your share] that you deny it?" He said: your thanks, you say: "We were rained upon by the star of such and such, and by the constellation of such and such."

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Bakr related to us, from Isra'il, from Abd al-A'la, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Ali, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: "And do you make your sustenance [your share] that you deny it?" He said: "Your thanks, that you deny," and he said: "They say: we were rained upon by the star of such and such."

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: No people were ever rained upon but that some of them became disbelievers in the morning, saying: "We were rained upon by the star of such and such." And Ibn Abbas recited: "And do you make your sustenance [your share] that you deny it?"

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Atiyya related to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Sulayman related to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, that he used to recite: "And do you make your sustenance [your share] that you deny it?" Then he said: No people were ever rained upon on any night but that some people became polytheists in the morning, saying: "We were rained upon by the star of such and such." He said: and he said: "And do you make your thanks that you deny."

Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning his words: "And do you make your sustenance": he means: your thanks for what He sent down upon you of rain and mercy, by saying: "We were rained upon by the star of such and such." He said: That was their disbelief in what God had bestowed upon them.

Yunus related to me, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Isma'il ibn Umayya, who said: I think it was he or someone else: that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, heard a man, when they were rained upon, say: "We were rained upon by some of the lions' thanwiyya [mansions of the moon]." He said: "You have lied; rather it is the provision of God."

* *

And His words: "Why then, when it reaches the throat"

He, exalted is His mention, says: Why not, when the souls reach, as they depart from your bodies, O people, your throats? "And you at that time are looking on" means: and those of you present among their kin look at them at that time. The address here is general to all, and what is meant is: those of the dead person's family and others who are present. This is well known in the speech of the Arabs: they address a group with a verb, as if they were his family and companions, while what is meant is some of them, absent or present, as one says: "You killed so-and-so," when only one of them, either absent or present, was the killer. We have explained parallels to this in many places in this book of ours.

He says: "And We are nearer to it than you": that is, Our messengers who seize its spirit are nearer to it than you. "But you do not see."

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: It is said, "Why then, when it reaches the throat, and you at that time are looking on," as if he had heard from them, and God knows best: "We are able not to die." So He said: "Why then, when it reaches the throat." Then He said: "Why then, if you are not to be recompensed," meaning: not requited, you return those souls while you see how it departs at that moment, if you are truthful that you can prevent death.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He: "Do you then treat this discourse with scorn? And do you make your sustenance [your share] that you deny it? Why then, when it [the soul] reaches the throat, and you at that time are looking on, and We are nearer to it than you, but you do not see."

Exalted is He says: Do you, O people, then soften your speech toward those who deny this Qur'an, of which I have informed you and whose matter I have related to you, out of complicity with them in denying it and disbelieving in it?

The exegetes differed in its interpretation. Some of them said, concerning it, something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of God: "Do you then treat this discourse with scorn?" He said: You wish to collude with them in it, and incline toward them.

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: "Do you then deny this discourse?"

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning his words: "Do you then treat this discourse with scorn?" He said: deniers, not believers.

I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning the words: "You are treating [it] with scorn." He said: deniers.

It has been mentioned from al-Haytham ibn Adi that among the dialect of the Azd Shanu'a is: "what [so-and-so] was provided" meaning "what [so-and-so] thanked."
