Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 56, verse 86–89:

Concerning the interpretation of His saying, ﴿Then why not, if you are not to be recompensed, ... (86) you would return it, if you are truthful? (87) But if he is of those brought near (to Allah), (88) then there is rest and provision and a Garden of Delight. (89)﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Then why not, if you, O people, are not to be held accountable (ghayr madinin)?"

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of His saying, ﴿madinin﴾. Some of them said: "Not called to account."

Mention of those who said that:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying, ﴿Then why not, if you are not to be recompensed﴾, he said: "Not called to account."

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿not to be recompensed﴾, he said: "Called to account."

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, ﴿Then why not, if you are not to be recompensed﴾: that is, "called to account."

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the saying of God, ﴿Then why not, if you are not to be recompensed﴾, he said: "They used to deny that they would be repaid after death." He said: "And He is Master of the Day of Judgment, the Day on which people are repaid for their deeds." He said: "Yudanun" means "they are called to account."

Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya related to us, saying: Abu Raja informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying, ﴿Then why not, if you are not to be recompensed﴾, he said: "Not called to account."

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Sulayman related to us, saying: Abu Hilal related to us, from Qatada, ﴿Then why not, if you are not to be recompensed﴾, he said: "Not resurrected, not called to account."

Others said: its meaning is: "not resurrected."

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Hawdha related to us, saying: Awf related to us, from al-Hasan, ﴿Then why not, if you are not to be recompensed﴾: "not resurrected on the Day of Resurrection; you would return it, if you are truthful."

Others said: rather, its meaning is: "not repaid for your deeds."

The most correct of these sayings in terms of truth is the saying of the one who said: "not called to account," and thus "repaid for your deeds," from their saying, "As you do, so you are repaid" (kama tadin tudan), and from the saying of Allah, ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾.

As for His saying, ﴿you would return it, if you are truthful﴾:

He says: you would return those souls, after their arrival at the throats (al-halaqim), to their resting place in the bodies, if you are truthful, if you are able to prevent death, reckoning and recompense. The answer to His saying, ﴿Then why not when it reaches the throat﴾, and the answer to His saying, ﴿Then why not, if you are not to be recompensed﴾, is one answer, namely His saying, ﴿you would return it﴾. This is like His saying, ﴿So if there comes to you guidance from Me, whoever follows My guidance, there will be no fear for them﴾; He made the answer of the two conditionals one answer.

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said concerning His saying, ﴿you would return it﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying, ﴿you would return it﴾, he said: "to that soul, ﴿if you are truthful﴾."

As for His saying, ﴿But if he is of those brought near﴾:

He says, may His remembrance be exalted: "But if the dead one is of those brought near, whom Allah has brought close into His neighborhood in His gardens, ﴿then there is rest and provision﴾," meaning: for him there is rest and provision.

The reciters differed in the recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of the regions recited ﴿farawhun﴾ with a fatha on the ra, meaning: for him there is coolness (bard). ﴿Wa-rayhan﴾ means: and wide provision according to some, and according to others: for him there is ease and sweet basil. Al-Hasan al-Basri recited it ﴿faruhun﴾ with a damma on the ra, meaning: that his spirit (ruh) departs in a sweet basil (rayhana).

The more correct of the two recitations in terms of truth is the recitation of the one who recited it with a fatha, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it, meaning: for him is mercy, forgiveness, and good, pleasant provision.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of His saying, ﴿farawhun wa-rayhan﴾. Some said: the meaning of that is: rest and a place of repose.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿farawhun wa-rayhan﴾: he said: "ease and a place of repose."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying, ﴿But if he is of those brought near, farawhun wa-rayhan﴾, he said: "By 'rayhan' is meant one who has found repose from the world." ﴿And a Garden of Delight﴾: he said: "forgiveness and mercy."

Others said: "rawh" is ease, and "rayhan" is provision.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿farawhun wa-rayhan﴾, he said: "ease," and His saying "rayhan," he said: "provision."

Others said: "al-rawh" is joy, and "al-rayhan" is provision.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Idris related to us, saying: I heard my father, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying, ﴿farawhun wa-rayhan﴾, he said: "al-rawh: joy, and al-rayhan: provision."

As for those who recited it with a damma on the ra, they said: "al-ruh" is the spirit of a human being, and "al-rayhan" is the well-known basil. They said the meaning of that is: the spirits of those brought near depart from their bodies at death with a basil which they smell.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir related to us, from his father, from al-Hasan, ﴿farawhun wa-rayhan﴾, he said: "his spirit departs in a basil."

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliya, ﴿But if he is of those brought near﴾, he said: "None of those brought near would depart from the world, and those brought near are the foremost, until there is brought to him a branch of the basil of Paradise, which he smells, and then he is taken."

Others who recited it with a fatha on the ra said: "al-rawh" is mercy, and "al-rayhan" is the well-known basil.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, ﴿farawhun wa-rayhan﴾, he said: "al-rawh: mercy, and al-rayhan: that which is received with at death."

Others among them said: "al-rawh" is mercy, and "al-rayhan" is relief.

Mention of those who said that:

It was related to me from al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, ﴿farawhun wa-rayhan﴾: "al-rawh: forgiveness and mercy, and al-rayhan: relief."

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Mundhir al-Thawri, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, ﴿But if he is of those brought near﴾, he said: "This is at death." ﴿farawhun wa-rayhan﴾, he said: "There is brought to him from Paradise."

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abu Amir related to us, saying: Qurra related to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying, ﴿But if he is of those brought near, farawhun wa-rayhan wa-jannatu na'im﴾, he said: "That is in the Hereafter." Then some of the people said to him: he said: "By God, indeed they see it at death."

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Hammad related to us, saying: Qurra related to us, from al-Hasan, similarly.

The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying of the one who said: by "al-rawh" is meant joy, mercy and forgiveness, and its origin is from their saying: "I found rawh," when one finds a breeze by which he is relieved from the distress of heat. As for "al-rayhan," in my view it is the basil with which one is received at death, as Abu al-Aliya and al-Hasan said, and whoever said similarly to them, because that is the most prevalent and most apparent of its meanings.

As for His saying, ﴿and a Garden of Delight﴾:

He says: and for him, in addition to that, is a garden of delight in which he enjoys himself.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "and a Garden of Delight," he said: "It has been shown to him."

Concerning the interpretation of His saying, ﴿Then why not, if you are not to be recompensed, ... (86) you would return it, if you are truthful? (87) But if he is of those brought near (to Allah), (88) then there is rest and provision and a Garden of Delight. (89)﴾

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said concerning His saying, ﴿you would return it﴾.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Mundhir al-Thawri, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, ﴿But if he is of those brought near﴾, he said: "This is at death." ﴿farawhun wa-rayhan﴾, he said: "There is brought to him from Paradise."

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abu Amir related to us, saying: Qurra related to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying, ﴿But if he is of those brought near, farawhun wa-rayhan wa-jannatu na'im﴾, he said: "That is in the Hereafter." Then some of the people said to him: he said: "By God, indeed they see it at death."

Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Hammad related to us, saying: Qurra related to us, from al-Hasan, similarly.

The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying of the one who said: by "al-rawh" is meant joy, mercy and forgiveness, and its origin is from their saying: "I found rawh," when one finds a breeze by which he is relieved from the distress of heat. As for "al-rayhan," in my view it is the basil with which one is received at death, as Abu al-Aliya and al-Hasan said, and whoever said similarly to them, because that is the most prevalent and most apparent of its meanings.

As for His saying, ﴿and a Garden of Delight﴾:

He says: and for him, in addition to that, is a garden of delight in which he enjoys himself.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "and a Garden of Delight," he said: "It has been shown to him."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 56, verses 90–94:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿But if he is of the companions of the right hand, then "Peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand."  And if he is of the deniers, the astray, then a welcome of boiling water, and roasting in Hellfire.﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And if he was﴾ the dead person ﴿of the companions of the right hand﴾, those who are taken to Paradise by their right side, ﴿then "Peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand."﴾

Then the interpreters differed regarding the meaning of His saying: ﴿"Peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand"﴾. The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said concerning it:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And if he was of the companions of the right hand, then "Peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand."﴾ He said: "Peace from Allah, and the angels of Allah greet him."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And if he was of the companions of the right hand * then "Peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand."﴾ He said: "Safe from what he dislikes."

As for the grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyyah), they differed regarding this. [[Most of the author's speech that he transmits from the grammarians here, from the Kufan grammarians, is from al-Farra's words in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 325 of the University's microfilm); he transmitted part of it verbatim and altered part of it in wording.]] Some of the Basran grammarians said, regarding ﴿And if he was of the companions of the right hand * then "Peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand."﴾: meaning, "It is said: 'Peace be upon you.'" Some of the Kufan grammarians said: As for His saying ﴿"Peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand"﴾: meaning, "Then that is affirmed for you, that you are of the companions of the right hand." The particle "an" (that) has been elided while its meaning is intended, just as you say: "You are believed, a traveler soon," when he has said: "I am a traveler soon," and so it is necessary that its meaning be: "You are a traveler soon, and believed soon." He said: And His saying ﴿"Peace be upon you"﴾ means: "So peace is upon you, you being of the companions of the right hand." He said: It may also be like a supplication for him, as in His saying: "So watering for you from the men" (fa-suqyan laka min al-rijal). He said: If you put "al-salam" in the nominative, it is a supplication, and God knows best what is correct.

Another of them said, regarding His saying ﴿"As for if he was of the brought near"﴾: he combined two answers, so that it is known that "amma" is a conditional. He said: As for His saying ﴿"Peace be upon you from the companions of the right hand"﴾, he said: The original of the phrase is "muslim laka hadha" (this is affirmed for you), then "an" was removed and "min" was placed in its position. He said: It has also been said: "Peace be upon you, you are of the companions of the right hand," so it is according to that: meaning "peace upon you," it is said: "You are of the companions of the right hand." All of this is on two statements.

He said: It has also been said: "muslim" (affirmed): meaning, just as you say, "fa-salam laka min al-qawm," as you say, "fa-suqyan laka min al-qawm," so it is one word.

The most correct of these sayings, in terms of truth, is that it is said: its meaning is: "Peace be upon you, that you are of the companions of the right hand." Then it was elided and what is indicated by "min" upon it was sufficed for, so he is safe from the punishment of Allah and from what he dislikes, because he is of the companions of the right hand.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this is the true certainty (ḥaqq al-yaqīn).﴾ ﴿So exalt the name of your Lord, the Mighty.﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Indeed, this that I have informed you of, O people, of the report concerning those brought near (al-muqarrabūn) and the companions of the right (aṣḥāb al-yamīn), and concerning the deniers, the astray, and what their affairs will lead to, ﴿indeed, it is the true certainty⦆ means: it is the truth of the certain report, without doubt.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wīl) said the same as what we have said about that.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Indeed, this is the true certainty⦆, he said: "The certain report."

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿But if he was among the deniers, the astray, then a welcome of boiling water, and burning in Hellfire. Indeed, this is the true certainty⦆, until the end of the verse: "Indeed, Allah, exalted is He, does not leave any of His creation until He makes them come to certainty about this Qur'an. As for the believer, he attains certainty in this world, and that benefits him on the Day of Resurrection. As for the disbeliever, he attains certainty on the Day of Resurrection when it does not benefit him."

The grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyyah) differed regarding the reason for the annexation of al-ḥaqq to al-yaqīn, when the truth is the certainty (al-ḥaqq al-yaqīn). Some of the grammarians of Basra said: "Ḥaqq al-yaqīn" — he annexed the truth to the certainty, as He said: ﴿And that is the religion of the upright (dīn al-qayyimah)⦆, meaning that is the religion of the upright community, and that is the true affair, the certain one. He said: "As for hādhā rajul al-sū' (this bad man), it would not be said of it in the way that it is said of ḥaqq al-yaqīn, because 'bad' (al-sū') is not a man, whereas certainty is the truth." Some of the people of Kufa said: "Al-yaqīn is a qualifier (na't) of al-ḥaqq, as if he said: 'the true, certain (al-ḥaqq al-yaqīn), and the upright religion (al-dīn al-qayyim)'. Something similar has come in much speech and in the Qur'an: ﴿And the abode of the Hereafter (wa-la-dār al-ākhirah)⦆ and ﴿the abode of the Hereafter (al-dār al-ākhirah)⦆." He said: "When it is annexed, one imagines it to be other than the first."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So exalt the name of your Lord, the Mighty⦆

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: So exalt the naming of your Lord, the Mighty, by His most beautiful names.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Waqi'ah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 56, verse 95–96:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this is the true certainty (ḥaqq al-yaqīn).﴾ ﴿So exalt the name of your Lord, the Mighty.﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Indeed, this that I have informed you of, O people, of the report concerning those brought near (al-muqarrabūn) and the companions of the right (aṣḥāb al-yamīn), and concerning the deniers, the astray, and what their affairs will lead to, ﴿indeed, it is the true certainty⦆ means: it is the truth of the certain report, without doubt.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wīl) said the same as what we have said about that.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Indeed, this is the true certainty⦆, he said: "The certain report."

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿But if he was among the deniers, the astray, then a welcome of boiling water, and burning in Hellfire. Indeed, this is the true certainty⦆, until the end of the verse: "Indeed, Allah, exalted is He, does not leave any of His creation until He makes them come to certainty about this Qur'an. As for the believer, he attains certainty in this world, and that benefits him on the Day of Resurrection. As for the disbeliever, he attains certainty on the Day of Resurrection when it does not benefit him."

The grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyyah) differed regarding the reason for the annexation of al-ḥaqq to al-yaqīn, when the truth is the certainty (al-ḥaqq al-yaqīn). Some of the grammarians of Basra said: "Ḥaqq al-yaqīn" — he annexed the truth to the certainty, as He said: ﴿And that is the religion of the upright (dīn al-qayyimah)⦆, meaning that is the religion of the upright community, and that is the true affair, the certain one. He said: "As for hādhā rajul al-sū' (this bad man), it would not be said of it in the way that it is said of ḥaqq al-yaqīn, because 'bad' (al-sū') is not a man, whereas certainty is the truth." Some of the people of Kufa said: "Al-yaqīn is a qualifier (na't) of al-ḥaqq, as if he said: 'the true, certain (al-ḥaqq al-yaqīn), and the upright religion (al-dīn al-qayyim)'. Something similar has come in much speech and in the Qur'an: ﴿And the abode of the Hereafter (wa-la-dār al-ākhirah)⦆ and ﴿the abode of the Hereafter (al-dār al-ākhirah)⦆." He said: "When it is annexed, one imagines it to be other than the first."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So exalt the name of your Lord, the Mighty⦆

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: So exalt the naming of your Lord, the Mighty, by His most beautiful names.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Waqi'ah.
